output.summary: KEP-2328 proposed adding instance metadata service (IMDS) support to cloud-controller-manager by introducing a cloud-node-manager daemonset that handles instance-level interfaces (Instances and Zones), so nodes can initialize from IMDS and reconcile IP addresses. The KEP is recorded as implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Moving node information retrieval to CCM made every node depend on cloud APIs, which are rate-limited and can throttle large clusters. The proposal keeps control-plane interfaces in CCM and moves instance-level interfaces to a daemonset, with an optional --enable-node-controller switch. The sources in this record do not show a design rationale for the implemented status itself; the discussion concerns how the status was set on PR #3007.

alternatives.option: Keep node initialization centralized in cloud-controller-manager (--enable-node-controller=true)
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this mode means CCM does all node initialization, which the proposal identifies as the source of cloud API throttling for large clusters.

alternatives.option: Introduce a separate cloud-provider plugin (CPI) registered into kubelet
alternatives.why_not: The readme says the plugin's daemonset would need to be schedulable before kubelet fully initialized nodes, requiring kubelet to initialize twice; separating it into cloud-node-manager was judged clearer.

evidence.quote: So the proposal aims to add IMDS support back with CCM, so that the kubernetes cluster could still be scaled to a large number of nodes.
For instance-level interfaces, a new daemonsets would be introduced and implement instance-level interfaces (who’s name is `cloud-node-manager`).
This KEP was initially declared implementable at alpha, before PRR was required. The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle.
